classification.difficultyReason: Reads coordinates, calculates the radius and considers either endpoint as the centre to form two circle equations.

content.prompt: Find the possible equations of a circle with radius $AB$.

spec.description: Equal-unit Cartesian grid with labelled points A and B, no joining segment and no axis arrowheads. Source point colours use the standard green and blue palette.
spec.mathematics: A=(2,-2), B=(5,2). Unit grid and numeric labels x=-1 to 7 and y=-3 to 3, including one zero at the origin.
spec.answerVisibility: The grid and both labelled points are permanent student-visible givens.

answer.worked:
The centre can be either endpoint of the radius $AB$.
$$\begin{align*}
AB&=\sqrt{(5-2)^2+(2-(-2))^2}\\
AB&=\sqrt{9+16}\\
AB&=5.
\end{align*}$$
With centre $A=(2,-2)$:
$$ (x-2)^2+(y+2)^2=25. $$
With centre $B=(5,2)$:
$$ (x-5)^2+(y-2)^2=25. $$
